source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-90: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 90 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat Mooncake-style remote KV as a measured systems hypothesis, not an automatic speedup. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but first record model and runtime versions, GPU/NIC models, PCIe and NUMA affinity, RDMA device and link capabilities, memory limits, topology/failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, cache warmness, and tenant policy. Unknown platform facts remain evidence_required rather than claims. This is Mooncake variant 05590; separate model-domain expectations from measurements.

Make ownership explicit: prefill workers construct KV and decode workers consume it. Document the block schema and precision, cache-key namespace, placement, replication, leases/epochs, version and checksum validation, TTL, eviction priority, admission quotas, and control-plane commit states. Authorization and tenant isolation must be checked before lookup. Reject stale, partial, corrupt, mismatched, or unauthorized blocks; never silently use them. For cache misses, RDMA timeouts, link errors, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, use a bounded local recompute or conventional-serving fallback, expose the event in traces, and define an operator-approved disable/rollback gate.

Falsifiable hypothesis: for a predeclared long-context workload at fixed concurrency and quality, remote KV reuse reduces prefill work enough to improve TTFT and throughput without worsening p95/p99 latency, error rate, cache-failure rate, memory pressure, or isolation incidents. Measure end-to-end latency and TTFT/TPOT, tokens/s, queueing, prefill/decode GPU time, bytes and operations transferred, RDMA lookup/transfer latency, cache hit/miss and eviction rates, retries, fallback rate, CPU/GPU/NIC utilization, memory, and errors, with units and synchronized timestamps.

Compare against (1) local KV recomputation and (2) a conventional distributed-serving baseline, matched for model, hardware, workload mix, batching, concurrency, cache state, warm-up, and SLO. Randomize or alternate runs, repeat enough to report uncertainty and tail percentiles, and isolate confounders such as placement, contention, compression, prompt reuse, and scheduler changes. For troubleshooting or tool use, correlate request traces with NIC counters, queue depth, application logs, health/lease state, and packet/error telemetry; validate causality with a controlled fault or canary, not a single symptom. Roll back or disable remote reuse when predefined latency/error/fallback or integrity thresholds are exceeded, and preserve audit logs. No improvement claim is warranted until these measurements and failure tests are available.

quality_dimensions.measurement: defines matched baselines, metrics, units, tails, repeats, and confounders

risks: Remote transfer or queueing may erase reuse benefit.

per-request traces with synchronized timestamps

matched local and conventional baselines with repeated trials and uncertainty
fault-injection or canary results for timeout, stale data, link, node, and control-plane failures

Make ownership explicit: prefill workers construct KV and decode workers consume it. Document the block schema and precision, cache-key namespace, placement, replication, leases/epochs, version and checksum validation, TTL, eviction priority, admission quotas, and control-plane commit states. Authorization and tenant isolation must be checked before lookup. Reject stale, partial, corrupt, mismatched, or unauthorized blocks; never silently use them. For cache misses, RDMA timeouts, link errors, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, use a bounded local recompute or conventional-serving fallback, expose the event in traces, and define an operator-approved disable/rollback gate.

Falsifiable hypothesis: for a predeclared long-context workload at fixed concurrency and quality, remote KV reuse reduces prefill work enough to improve TTFT and throughput without worsening p95/p99 latency, error rate, cache-failure rate, memory pressure, or isolation incidents. Measure end-to-end latency and TTFT/TPOT, tokens/s, queueing, prefill/decode GPU time, bytes and operations transferred, RDMA lookup/transfer latency, cache hit/miss and eviction rates, retries, fallback rate, CPU/GPU/NIC utilization, memory, and errors, with units and synchronized timestamps.

Compare against (1) local KV recomputation and (2) a conventional distributed-serving baseline, matched for model, hardware, workload mix, batching, concurrency, cache state, warm-up, and SLO. Randomize or alternate runs, repeat enough to report uncertainty and tail percentiles, and isolate confounders such as placement, contention, compression, prompt reuse, and scheduler changes. For troubleshooting or tool use, correlate request traces with NIC counters, queue depth, application logs, health/lease state, and packet/error telemetry; validate causality with a controlled fault or canary, not a single symptom. Roll back or disable remote reuse when predefined latency/error/fallback or integrity thresholds are exceeded, and preserve audit logs. No improvement claim is warranted until these measurements and failure tests are available.
